target.title: perf(gateway): replace O(n^2) char loop with regex in stripDisallowedChatControlChars
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #102915 — `stripDisallowedChatControlChars` iterates over every character
of the message rebuilding the string with `+=` concatenation. For messages
containing large datasets or files (1MB+), this blocks the event loop for
significant duration. On a 1MB message the old implementation takes ~128ms
(blocking), while the regex replacement takes ~2ms (71× speedup).

## Why This Change Was Made

The character loop is O(n²) in practice due to immutable string concatenation.
A single regex replace is O(n) and scans the string once. The regex
`/[\x00-\x08\x0B\x0C\x0E-\x1F\x7F]/g` matches the exact same set of disallowed
control characters as the original conditional, verified character-by-character.

## User Impact

**Before:** 1MB chat message → event loop blocked for ~128ms, gateway
unresponsive during sanitization.

**After:** 1MB chat message → sanitized in ~2ms, no perceptible event-loop
blocking.

## Evidence

Branch: `fix/102915-strip-control-chars-perf` | Base: `upstream/main` | Node: v22.19.0 Linux x64

### Regression tests

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/chat-input-sanitize.test.ts --reporter=verbose

 ✓ strips disallowed control characters (NUL–BS, VT, FF, SO–US, DEL)
 ✓ preserves tab, newline, and carriage return
 ✓ preserves printable ASCII and Unicode characters
 ✓ rejects null byte via sanitizeChatSendMessageInput
 ✓ returns empty string when the message consists entirely of disallowed characters
 ✓ returns the input unchanged when no disallowed characters are present
 ✓ strips DEL (127) which is the boundary between control and printable ASCII
 ✓ preserves the full printable ASCII range (32–126)

 Test Files  4 passed (4)
      Tests  32 passed (32)
   Duration  2.19s
```

### Live proof: `node --import tsx` production function

```
$ node --import tsx -e "import { sanitizeChatSendMessageInput } from ./src/gateway/chat-input-sanitize.js;

const r = sanitizeChatSendMessageInput(hx01ello);
console.log(r.ok && r.message === hello ? PASS : FAIL);
// PASS
const r2 = sanitizeChatSendMessageInput(testx00nul);
console.log(!r2.ok ? PASS : FAIL);
// PASS
const r3 = sanitizeChatSendMessageInput(beforex7Fafter);
console.log(r3.message === beforeafter ? PASS : FAIL);
// PASS"
```

### Live proof: performance benchmark

```
$ node --import tsx -e "<benchmark>"

Message size: 1024 KB
Old (for...of +=): 127.5 ms
New (regex): 1.8 ms
Speedup: 71.1×
Correctness: PASS (identical output)
Event loop blocked (old): YES - 0.1s
Event loop blocked (new): NO
```

### Checks

- `oxfmt --check` — passed
- `oxlint` — passed
- `git diff --check` — passed
- `autoreview --engine claude` — **patch is correct (1)**, no findings

### Diff summary

```
src/gateway/chat-input-sanitize.ts      | 16 ++++-- (regex constant + replace)
src/gateway/chat-input-sanitize.test.ts | 61 ++++++ (8 regression cases)
```

- [x] I understand what the code does
- [x] Change is focused and does not mix unrelated concerns
